anchor: 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL in the deterministic suite ... this is the *weakest* outcome, not the strongest.
statement: Deterministic suite across 10 scenarios x 20 properties yields 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL(CIRC-5)/2 DEFINITIONAL, but the report explicitly warns this is the weakest evidence in the paper because deterministic passes can be vacuous.

anchor: AD-1 highly probable but false claim ... FAIL — CE-1 ... AD-18 conclusion with no supporting evidence ... FAIL — CE-2 (positive control)
statement: Adversarial suite: AD-1 attributes os=RHEL9.8 against true RHEL8.6 (CE-1 factivity failure); AD-18's injected unsupported conclusion is caught by P10 yet still attributed (CE-2 positive-control failure, since attribution never checks provenance).

anchor: P11 | 0.3394 ... 420 | 0.1237 ... P3's guard never activated ... Its 100% pass is vacuous and must not be cited
statement: Randomized layer (10,000 trials, 5 seeds x 2000): P11's guard activates in 33.94% of trials with 420 failures (conditional failure rate 0.1237); P3's guard never activates so its 100% pass rate is vacuous and excluded from evidence.

anchor: a source rated reliable reported a **false** value | **414 / 665** | **0.6226** ... Every violation is explained by the epistemic state being unable to distinguish a reliable-looking false report from a true one.
statement: Factivity diagnosis: conditional on an attribution being made, violation rate is 0.6226 (414/665) when a policy-trusted source reported a false value versus 0/2607 otherwise, interpreted as 'the witness in A at scale' rather than a tuning problem.

anchor: I would separate the theory into three distinct layers ... PHILOSOPHICAL / CONCEPTUAL MODEL ... EPISTEMIC MATHEMATICAL MODEL ... DDD DOMAIN MODEL ... ARCHITECTURAL REALIZATION ... The new methodology explicitly forbids that inference.
statement: Proposes making a four-layer separation (Philosophical -> Epistemic Mathematical -> DDD Domain -> Architectural Realization) constitutional in Theory v1.2, explicitly forbidding the direct inference chain Gita concept -> mathematical concept -> primitive -> DDD object -> architecture.

anchor: id(K)=H(P,e,c,t,\Pi) does not mean K_1=K_2 and certainly does not mean K_1\equiv K_2 ... rather than allowing them to collapse into "knowledge identity".
statement: Argues Theory v1.2 must explicitly separate Identity, Equality, Semantic equivalence, Observational equivalence, and Provenance-sensitive equivalence, restating 'no one of these may silently substitute for another' as a required section rather than an implicit habit.

anchor: K_t = ratified KnowledgeOS state representation ... while O_core, delta, equiv, approx, cong_lambda remain partially unresolved ... This is exactly why Step 261 remains an overarching gate.
statement: Recommends K_t be downgraded from an assumed-complete operational kernel to merely a 'ratified state representation', with the operational core (O_core, delta, equivalence relations) explicitly left unresolved pending Step 261.

anchor: Observation = OPEN CONCEPT ... rather than: Observation = (x,t,c,s). The latter should be labelled: Candidate Observation Model
statement: Recommends downgrading Observation from a v1.1 definition O_t=(x,t,c,s) to an OPEN CONCEPT with that tuple relabelled a Candidate Observation Model, pending Step 291.

anchor: Buddhi is a philosophical lens for investigating discrimination/determination ... corroboration != derivation.
statement: Demotes Buddhi from 'KnowledgeOS decision function' to a philosophical lens motivating (not deriving) a discrimination-capability requirement, restating the Step-286 methodological principle 'corroboration != derivation'.

anchor: Zero = candidate epistemic-boundary construct ... investigate whether Zero is actually: a state; a relation; a predicate; a boundary; a derived view; a missingness representation; or merely a conceptual metaphor.
statement: Reclassifies Zero from a defined construct to a 'candidate epistemic-boundary construct' and poses the open question of which ontological category (state/relation/predicate/boundary/derived view/missingness representation/metaphor) it belongs to -- the question later research in this batch investigates directly.

anchor: Define provisionally: E_t = epistemic configuration available to a knower ... K_t = KnowledgeOS governed knowledge state. ... E_t \neq K_t as a research distinction, not yet as a fully ratified ontological theorem.
statement: Introduces Epistemic State (E_t, potentially containing observations, beliefs, hypotheses, alternatives, uncertainty) as distinct from the governed Knowledge State (K_t), proposed as a research distinction rather than a ratified theorem.

anchor: I would restructure KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 ... I. Philosophical orientation ... XI. DDD Architecture
statement: Proposes an eleven-part restructured table of contents for KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 (Philosophical orientation, Methodology, Reality/Knowledge Space, Epistemic model, Knowledge State, Identity and Equality, Operations, Epistemic evolution, Governance, Philosophical lenses, DDD Architecture).

anchor: ESTABLISHED | directly demonstrated or ratified ... UNKNOWN | insufficient evidence ... This would prevent the exact problems we encountered in Steps 285-288.
statement: Proposes an eleven-value epistemic status vocabulary (ESTABLISHED, DERIVED, BOUNDED, HYPOTHESIS, INTERPRETATION, CORROBORATION, NORMATIVE, TECHNICALLY OPEN, DEFERRED, REFUTED, UNKNOWN) to be applied throughout v1.2, later adopted verbatim across the batch's simulation and Zero artifacts.

anchor: I would not discard v1.1 ... Theory v1.1 = valid architectural baseline ... Theory v1.1 != closed epistemic theory ... I can write that full reconciliation prompt as the next controlled research mandate.
statement: Final assessment: Theory v1.1 remains a valid architectural baseline but not a closed epistemic theory; recommends commissioning a controlled v1.1->v1.2 reconciliation producing a claim-by-claim matrix (v1.1 claim -> current evidence -> Step 285-290 impact -> KEEP/NARROW/RECLASSIFY/SUPERSEDE/OPEN -> proposed v1.2 wording) rather than a hand rewrite.

anchor: No total Gamma : (E,Q,C,EC) -> K that attributes anything is factive | DERIVED PROPOSITION, witness-supported ... not yet written as a theorem in the theory document
statement: Grades the factivity-impossibility claim as a derived, witness-supported proposition whose general one-line argument (Gamma's domain excludes truth) has not yet been written as a formal theorem in the theory document.

anchor: equiv_sem is well defined | STILL REQUIRING MATHEMATICAL WORK | CIRC-5 -- currently circular
statement: Records semantic equivalence's well-definedness as STILL REQUIRING MATHEMATICAL WORK, citing CIRC-5's circularity.

anchor: Kernel minimality | NOT ADDRESSED -- deliberately | Section 13 of the protocol; see K
statement: Records kernel minimality as deliberately not addressed per the protocol's explicit prohibition on operator counting.

anchor: Revision requires an evidence-retirement relation | DERIVED FROM A NEGATIVE RESULT | CE-3 -- the theory has none, and the omission is load-bearing
statement: States the need for an evidence-retirement relation is itself derived from CE-3's negative result: the theory's silence on retirement is load-bearing, not incidental.

anchor: Any of this describes real knowledge | STILL REQUIRING EMPIRICAL VALIDATION | the world is synthetic; nothing here is evidence about actual epistemic practice
statement: Explicitly grades every simulation result as providing no empirical evidence about real epistemic practice, since the tested world is synthetic.

anchor: The non-circularity and the impossibility are the same fact. Because truth never re-enters the agent's state, Gamma cannot consult it -- which is exactly why CE-1 occurs.
statement: CIRC-1 (Knowledge-via-Truth / Truth-via-Knowledge) is found NOT circular, and this non-circularity is identified as the same underlying fact that produces CE-1: World.truth is exogenous and no agent transition reads it, so Gamma structurally cannot be factive.

anchor: Adequate (DEF-20) and Zero (DEF-22) are extensionally identical ... In the implementation Adequate is literally 'return Zero(...)'.
statement: CIRC-3 finds Adequate and Zero extensionally identical (both reduce to Delta_t=empty) -- classified a redundancy rather than a circularity, with two open repairs proposed.

anchor: P7 compares two representations' behaviour under a semantic projection sem(K) = (status, A, attributed, value) -- chosen by the experimenter. ... it is why that lane's minimal kernel was 13 under one algebra and 8 under another.
statement: CIRC-5 finds P7's semantic-equivalence test circular: the projection defining 'behaviour' was chosen by the experimenter with no independent criterion, explicitly linked to why the prior kernel-reduction lane got two different minimal-kernel sizes under two algebras.

anchor: The theory's own epistemic preservation vector P = (Meaning, Evidence, Warrant, Uncertainty, Alternatives, History, Identity, Context, Inquiry, Authorization) (Section 66) is a candidate: fix P first, by contract ... Not tested here.
statement: Proposes fixing the theory's declared epistemic preservation vector by contract as a candidate independent grounding for semantic equivalence, explicitly not tested in this pass.

anchor: TG-1 | DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 equation K = Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any attributing Gamma | G3 epistemological | CE-1; witness; 420/10000 randomized violations | CRITICAL
statement: Registers TG-1 (CRITICAL, G3 epistemological class): the factivity/attribution-equation impossibility, evidenced by the CE-1 witness and 420/10000 randomized violations.

anchor: R1 -- Rename the object ... R2 -- Make factivity external ... R3 -- Make Gamma partial ... The choice is a theory decision, not an experimental one. This lane does not make it.
statement: Presents three unchosen repairs for TG-1 -- R1 rename K_t to attributed knowledge, R2 make factivity an externally-verified success condition no component may assert, R3 make Gamma partial (attribute only where externally verifiable) -- explicitly declaring the choice a theory/governance decision outside this experiment's scope.

anchor: TG-2 | No evidence-retirement relation: Revise exists, Supersede/Retract/Expire do not | G2 semantic | CE-3 | HIGH
statement: Registers TG-2 (HIGH, G2 semantic): the missing evidence-retirement relation, evidenced by CE-3.

anchor: TG-4 | equiv_sem is defined via behaviour, behaviour via a chosen projection | G1 mathematical | CIRC-5 | HIGH -- blocks minimality
statement: Registers TG-4 (HIGH, blocks minimality): the CIRC-5 circular-projection problem for semantic equivalence.

anchor: TG-13 | The kernel shape (P, R, delta, I, U) proposed by the prior lane was not tested | G8 architectural | out of scope | MEDIUM
statement: Registers TG-13: the prior kernel-reduction lane's proposed kernel shape (preservation vector, relations, transition function, invariants, uncertainty) was never tested by this simulation, kept explicitly out of scope.

anchor: No operator count is reported. The protocol forbids it and the previous lane (KR-2026-09-01, THM-10) established that operator-count minimality is representation-relative: the same capability set admitted a 13-operator and an 8-operator minimum under two different algebras.
statement: Declines to report an operator count, citing the protocol's ban and the prior kernel-reduction lane's THM-10 finding that minimality is representation-relative (13 vs 8 operators under two algebras).

anchor: world-contact | nothing else can introduce empirical content (SMUG-0) ... authorization | decision made, permission withheld (P16)
statement: Enumerates thirteen externally-distinguishable epistemic capabilities (world-contact, evidential admission, meaning assignment, hypothesis-space opening, target-relative assessment, set-valued selection, elimination, attribution, state commit, normative comparison, closure judgment, action preference, authorization), each backed by an observable distinguishing behaviour.

anchor: Adequate <- Zero | SUPPORTED -- extensionally identical (CIRC-3); one is redundant ... Evidence <- Observation | REFUTED -- admission policy can exclude a source
statement: Tests seven candidate operator reductions: only Adequate<-Zero is SUPPORTED (redundant per CIRC-3); Determination<-Knowledge, Decision<-Determination, Authorization<-Decision, Action<-Authorization, Underdetermined<-Unobservable and Evidence<-Observation are all REFUTED by explicit counterexample.

anchor: Until equiv_sem is grounded independently (candidate: the preservation vector P, fixed by contract), no minimality claim is admissible.
statement: States plainly that no minimality claim about the kernel is admissible until CIRC-5's semantic-equivalence circularity is independently resolved.

anchor: The theory executes the whole epistemic lifecycle and keeps every distinction it declares -- except that DEF-1 (factivity) and the v1.1 attribution equation K = Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) cannot both hold. Theory status: B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE.
statement: States the one-line headline result for the whole v1.1 simulation lane and its Theory Status verdict (B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE), restated from the FINAL-VERDICT artifact.

anchor: Status [EXP] -- simulation of the theory, not of the product. Not canonical architecture, not a production implementation, not a final kernel, not a proven theory, not a validated ontology.
statement: Explicitly disclaims canonical, production, kernel, proof, or ontology status for the entire simulation lane, framing it strictly as a simulation of the theory.

anchor: DEF-1 (factivity) and the v1.1 attribution equation are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything ... The only escaping policy attributes nothing.
statement: Restates the factivity-impossibility as established, adding that the only Gamma escaping the contradiction attributes nothing at all.

anchor: Determination is genuinely set-valued. |A| = 0, 1, >1 are three observably different outcomes, and Reject(H1) never produced Accept(H2).
statement: Establishes that determination is genuinely set-valued (zero, one, or many admissible answers are three distinct observable outcomes) and that rejection never silently produces acceptance of an alternative.

anchor: CE-3 -- revision without retraction. Revise leaves superseded evidence at full weight, driving a changing world monotonically toward permanent underdetermination.
statement: Restates CE-3 as a theory failure (not implementation failure): Revise's lack of an evidence-retirement mechanism drives a changing world toward permanent underdetermination.

anchor: B. PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE ... A theory with two clauses that are jointly unsatisfiable is not "internally coherent under tested conditions"; it is executable everywhere except at the point where it says what knowledge is.
statement: Delivers and justifies the Theory Status verdict B (PARTIALLY EXECUTABLE): not A (inconsistent, since the contradiction is localized with three available repairs), not C, not D, and explicitly distinguishing localized-but-fatal incoherence from general incoherence.

anchor: The Factivity Repair Experiment. Implement all three repairs from L ... as three arms over the same scenarios and the same 10,000 worlds ... Do not run another large randomized simulation first.
statement: Prescribes the Factivity Repair Experiment as the mandatory next step: run R1/R2/R3 as three arms over the identical 10,000 worlds, explicitly forbidding another large randomized run before this.

anchor: The single most consequential change is three-valued Sat: it makes v1.1's sentence "Zero <=> Delta_t = empty" ambiguous. That one sentence names three different predicates, and they disagree on the most important case.
statement: States the executive finding of the v1.2 run: three-valued class-indexed Sat makes v1.1's single Zero definition name three disagreeing predicates.

anchor: A state where everything the agent could determine is determined and corroborated is not Zero (strict), is Zero (weak), and undetermined (Kleene). The three undetermined requirements are governance, temporal and operational -- exactly the three classes v1.2 itself marks open.
statement: Details result 1 (E1): the fully determined/corroborated case gives strict=false, weak=true, Kleene=U, and the U-producing classes are exactly the three the theory itself marks open, so Zero's evaluability is gated by the theory's own unresolved items.

anchor: state | REFUTED ... missingness representation | REFUTED -- all four unknown kinds collapse to U; Zero is coarser than the missingness taxonomy ... boundary | SUPPORTED only under three-valued Sat
statement: Details result 2 (E5): of Zero's seven v1.2-declared candidate readings, 'state' and 'missingness representation' are refuted, 'predicate'/'boundary'/'derived view' are supported with conditions, and 'metaphor' is not refuted.

anchor: 13 of 20 ordered pairs are separable by an explicit witness. The 7 that are not form a refinement order ... But the order is lambda-relative.
statement: Details result 3 (E2): the five equality relations form a refinement implication order in 7 of 20 pairs (the rest genuinely non-substitutable), and the order itself moves with the observation window lambda.

anchor: Both v1.1 failures persist -- and v1.2 makes one of them better reported. ... v1.2 splits into 1 violated (rs) + 6 undetermined. The failure is identical; the report is strictly more informative.
statement: Details result 4 (E3): CE-1 factivity and CE-3 revision both persist under v1.2 unrepaired, but three-valued Sat improves diagnostic resolution (splitting one undifferentiated gap into 1 violated + 6 undetermined).

anchor: Every corroboration-dependent conclusion in this programme rests on a component of a concept v1.2 declares OPEN. ... Dropping the source component collapses corroboration and flips every downstream result.
statement: Details result 5 (E4): dropping the observation model's source component collapses corroboration and flips determination/attribution/Zero, showing corroboration-dependent conclusions rest on a component the theory itself calls OPEN.

anchor: Zero is coarser than the missingness taxonomy | REFUTED (as a missingness representation) | E5 -- all four unknown kinds map to U
statement: Applies REFUTED-as-a-reading status specifically to 'Zero as missingness representation', distinguishing it from other Zero readings that survive.

anchor: The one gap in the vocabulary: it has no term for "refuted as one reading, surviving as another", which is exactly Zero's situation in E5. REFUTED is currently all-or-nothing.
statement: Identifies a gap in the v1.2 epistemic-status vocabulary itself: no status exists to express that a construct is refuted under one reading while surviving under another, which Zero's E5 result exactly requires.

anchor: Applying v1.2's status vocabulary was the cheapest and highest-yield change in this run. It forced a distinction the v1.1 lane had to make in prose.
statement: Assesses that applying the v1.2 status vocabulary was the single cheapest, highest-yield methodological change of the whole run, forcing distinctions previously left to prose.

anchor: The v1.2 run reuses the entire v1.1 pipeline unchanged, and replaces only the evaluation layer ... any difference between the v1.1 and v1.2 results is attributable to the theory, not to the simulator.
statement: Describes the controlled-experiment design: the v1.1 pipeline (world, state, transitions) is reused byte-identical, so any difference between v1.1 and v1.2 results is attributable to the theory change, not the simulator.

anchor: Gap is no longer a set. It is a partition: GapPartition(K, Req) = (violated, undetermined, satisfied) ... Zero_strict(g) <=> violated=empty AND undetermined=empty ... Zero_kleene(g) in {top,bot,U}
statement: Formalizes the consequence of three-valued Sat: Gap becomes a three-way partition (violated/undetermined/satisfied), producing three distinct candidate Zero definitions (strict, weak, Kleene) from the single prior equation.

anchor: E1 | Do the three Zero readings ever disagree? | Yes -- on the fully determined case. ... E5 | What kind of thing is Zero, of the seven v1.2 candidates? | 2 refuted, 1 partial, 4 surviving
statement: Tabulates the five formal experiments (E1 Zero-reading disagreement, E2 equality substitutability, E3 CE-1/CE-3 persistence, E4 OPEN-observation dependence, E5 which of seven Zero readings survive) with their one-line results.

experiment.hypothesis: the three-valued Sat weakening of v1.1 changes, worsens, or better-diagnoses the prior theory's failures
experiment.setup: reuse v1.1 pipeline, replace only the evaluation layer with class-indexed three-valued Sat
experiment.assumptions: 8 requirement classes exhaustive; status order cannot-determine<underdetermined<unique; no explicit governance authority supplied; lambda=(status,value) unless stated; delta undefined
experiment.inputs: same 10 scenario families and 10000 randomized worlds as v1.1
experiment.method: run E1-E5 as five targeted deterministic/derived experiments, not a new randomized layer
experiment.result: three Zero readings disagree; 13/20 equality pairs form a refinement order; CE-1/CE-3 persist; corroboration hostage to OPEN observation model; 2 Zero readings refuted
experiment.interpretation: the weakening was scientifically productive though it repaired no failure
experiment.limitations: synthetic world; 8-class exhaustiveness untested; lambda choice arbitrary
experiment.conclusion: Theory status B, same as v1.1, for different (more honest) reasons

anchor: governance requires an explicit authority; none was supplied | supplying one moves rg from U to top/bot and would make Zero_strict reachable ... delta is undefined (Step 290 open) | defining it moves ro out of U
statement: Declares the assumptions underlying the v1.2 run and their sensitivity: no governance authority supplied (keeps Zero_strict unreachable), lambda fixed to (status,value), delta left undefined per Step 290.

assumptions.statement: governance requires an explicit authority; none was supplied
delta (operation semantics) is undefined per Step 290 open status

anchor: TG12-1 | Zero <=> Delta=empty is ambiguous under three-valued Sat -- it names 3 predicates that disagree | G1 mathematical | NORMATIVE decision required | CRITICAL
statement: Registers TG12-1 (CRITICAL): Zero's three-way ambiguity under three-valued Sat, requiring a normative (not experimental) decision.

anchor: The weakening was productive. v1.2 did not repair a single v1.1 failure -- but it made two of them better diagnosed, exposed one defect v1.1's phrasing had hidden (Zero's ambiguity), and gave the programme a vocabulary in which "we do not know" is a first-class result rather than a hedge.
statement: Delivers the comparison verdict: v1.2 repaired no v1.1 failure but improved diagnosis of two, exposed a hidden defect (Zero's ambiguity) v1.1's phrasing had concealed, and made 'unknown' a first-class result.

anchor: E_t != K_t was a correction in v1.1 and is a research distinction in v1.2. ... v1.2 has no ratified statement that the contradiction contradicts. The failure is now homeless: real, reproducible, and attached to a claim the theory no longer asserts firmly.
statement: Identifies the one thing v1.2 made strictly worse: downgrading E_t!=K_t to a research distinction leaves the CE-1 contradiction 'homeless' -- real and reproducible but no longer attached to a firmly-asserted claim.

anchor: Zero_strict was unreachable in every case tested ... because governance, temporal and operational requirements are permanently U. Under the strict reading, no state this experiment could construct is ever Zero.
statement: Establishes that Zero_strict is unreachable in every constructed case because three requirement classes are permanently U by construction.

anchor: NOT TESTED -- and under v1.2, not testable. ... A kernel cannot be selected while its operation semantics are open, and E1 shows even the closure predicate itself is ambiguous. This is v1.2 behaving correctly, not a shortfall of the experiment.
statement: Delivers a stronger kernel-status verdict than v1.1: not merely untested but not-yet-testable under v1.2's own declared openness of operation semantics and closure predicate.

anchor: The weakening was scientifically productive: v1.2 repaired no failure but exposed a defect v1.1's phrasing had concealed, and improved the diagnosis of one it inherited.
statement: Restates the productive-weakening thesis as the closing verdict of the v1.2 lane.

anchor: The Zero Closure Decision Experiment. Three arms, one per reading ... supply a governance authority and a temporal semantics for the test harness -- E1 shows those two classes alone are responsible for Zero_strict never being reachable.
statement: Prescribes the Zero Closure Decision Experiment (three arms, one per reading) as next, with governance authority and temporal semantics supplied as prerequisites -- a plan later superseded by the Sat_c-first sequencing correction in this same batch.

anchor: R3 as specified does not repair factivity. 0.1181 against a baseline of 0.1175 -- indistinguishable, and marginally worse. It buys nothing and costs 66% of coverage. ... Partiality by availability is not partiality by warrant
statement: Finding 1: R3 (partial Gamma restricted to verifiable properties) fails to repair factivity while costing 66% of coverage, because verifiability-by-availability is orthogonal to whether the reporting source is misleading.

anchor: R3' repairs factivity by ceasing to be an epistemic system. ... 71.2% of R3's attributions are not products of the epistemic pipeline. R3' does not repair the epistemic system; it bypasses it.
statement: Finding 2: a corrected R3' (which actually consults an external verification channel) achieves zero factivity violations, but 71.2% of its attributions bypass the epistemic pipeline entirely, and it violates the premise the impossibility theorem depends on (Gamma is no longer a function of evidence alone).

anchor: R1 and R2 are behaviourally identical. Every number matches to the unit ... R2's useful measurement: of the claims the kernel emits, 2930/3320 = 88.25% survive external verification.
statement: Finding 3: R1 (rename) and R2 (externalize) are numerically identical but architecturally different; R2's externalization uniquely makes an 88.25% external-verification survival rate measurable.

anchor: Two of the three proposed repairs work, and they are the same intervention: stop calling it knowledge. ... it removes the blocker the review named ... Sat should therefore stay [PROP]
statement: Verdict: R1 and R2 are the genuine repairs and share one intervention (stop calling attribution knowledge); the experiment removes the factivity-based objection to defining Sat but Sat should remain [PROP] for other, independent reasons (Zero's three-way ambiguity, undefined status order, unproven class exhaustiveness).

anchor: Sat(K_t,r) in {top,bot,U} where top=established satisfied; bot=established violated; U=cannot currently be determined. That third value is important. Unknown must not silently become false.
statement: Defines the core three-valued satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r) and states the guiding principle that Unknown must never silently collapse into False.

anchor: R = R_content U R_evidence U R_provenance U R_epistemic U R_consistency U R_governance U R_temporal U R_operational ... Sat(K_t,r) = Sat_c(K_t,r) if r in R_c
statement: Partitions the requirement universe into eight classes (content, evidence, provenance, epistemic-status, consistency, governance, temporal, operational) and makes Sat class-indexed rather than one universal predicate.

anchor: p notin Content(K_t) does not necessarily mean not-p in Content(K_t). Absence is not negation. ... Evidence existence != evidence sufficiency ... Evidence != Truth.
statement: States two foundational non-collapse distinctions for the content and evidence classes: absence is not negation, and evidence existence is not evidence sufficiency, evidence is not truth.

anchor: the review says: Strong candidate [DEF] Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U}. I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface ... because our latest simulation has already exposed a fundamental issue: factivity vs Gamma-determinacy.
statement: First self-review downgrades Sat from a proposed [DEF] to [PROP], citing the v1.1 factivity/Gamma-determinacy impossibility as the reason it cannot yet be mathematically closed.

anchor: We have not yet derived Sat; we have derived the need for a satisfaction mechanism. ... K_t, r, Gamma_t -[evaluation semantics]-> epistemic evaluation -> Delta_t ... investigating whether that evaluation can legitimately be represented by {top,bot,U}.
statement: Second self-review (a meta-review of the first) sharpens the distinction further: only the need for a satisfaction mechanism has been derived, not Sat itself; recommends investigating an evaluation-semantics object before assuming the three-valued codomain.

anchor: The eight definitions I gave previously are therefore still useful. But I would now label them: Sat_c Formal Candidate Specification v0.1 -- not implementation. ... we absolutely can define all eight Sat_c functions now without implementing them.
statement: Establishes the 'define != implement' discipline that governs the rest of the Sat_c research thread: specify the eight class functions as a v0.1 candidate without writing executable code for them.

anchor: U ├── epistemic U ... ├── theory U ├── NO_EVALUATOR ├── NO_ORDERING ... └── world U └── UNOBSERVABLE ... That is potentially more important than the eight classes themselves.
statement: Proposes a three-branch taxonomy of the value U itself -- epistemic U (agent doesn't know), theory U (no evaluator exists), world U (unobservable) -- judged potentially more important than the eight requirement classes.

anchor: the satisfaction family has no place to attach truth. ... If KnowledgeOS intends satisfaction to support a truth-bearing notion of knowledge, the current satisfaction family contains no semantic attachment point for that relation.
statement: Endorses A-2 as the strongest finding of the run, restating it more precisely: the defect is structural (no attachment point for truth in the satisfaction family), not an accident of any particular evaluator.

anchor: PB-4 is probably the most important operational result ... more requirements -> more class evaluations -> more opportunities for blocked evaluation -> U propagation -> closure becomes impossible. ... Kleene conjunction faithfully exposes semantic incompleteness.
statement: Reframes PB-4 (blocked-class contagion) as evidence that Kleene conjunction is working correctly by faithfully propagating unresolved semantics, not as a defect of the composition rule.

anchor: I would rename the next experiment: Sat_c Specification Repair & Evaluator Completion Experiment ... Gate 1 -- Repair, without implementation ... Gate 5 -- Ask the decisive question
statement: Recommends a five-gate 'Sat_c Specification Repair & Evaluator Completion Experiment' sequencing PB-2/PB-3/PB-5 repair before candidate governance/temporal/operational evaluators are introduced, keeping the eventual Zero choice a theory/governance decision.

anchor: I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U} ... So we cannot yet say that Sat has been mathematically closed.
statement: Downgrades the proposed Sat definition from a strong candidate [DEF] to [PROP] because the factivity-vs-Gamma-determinacy obstruction has not yet been repaired.

anchor: The next step should be the Factivity Repair Experiment: R1 -- rename K_t ... R2 -- externalize factivity ... R3 -- make Gamma partial ... Do not start another large random experiment yet.
statement: Directly commissions the Factivity Repair Experiment (R1/R2/R3 over the same scenarios/worlds), which Experiment E (S2403) subsequently runs.

anchor: 3-valued semantics: candidate and 4-valued semantics: hypothesis/question rather than choosing either now.
statement: Declines to choose between three-valued and four-valued (contradiction-inclusive) satisfaction semantics, keeping both explicitly open pending further research.

anchor: Only 3 of 8 classes are executable now ... status | Contr undefined; whether contradiction needs a 4th value is OPEN ... governance | no evaluator exists -- this is why every governance requirement read U in E1
statement: A-1: specifying (not implementing) the eight Sat_c classes reveals only 3 (content, evidence, provenance) are executable; status/consistency/governance/temporal/operational are each blocked by a named specific missing evaluator or undefined relation, explaining why E1 produced permanent U for those classes.

anchor: No class in the family requires factivity. ... A knowledge state can satisfy all eight classes and still be false. CE-1 is therefore not an accident of Gamma: the satisfaction family has no place to attach truth.
statement: A-2: none of the eight satisfaction classes carries any factivity requirement, so full satisfaction never entails truth -- a stronger, specification-level restatement of CE-1's mechanism.

anchor: Sat_content returns top if p in Content(K) and bot if not-p in Content(K). Both can hold. The codomain {top,bot,U} has no value for it, so Sat_content is not a function on such states.
statement: PB-2: Sat_content is not total under contradiction (both p and not-p present), since the codomain has no value for that case; three repairs are possible but none is chosen.

anchor: blocked-class contagion: the decisive result. Every composite requirement of arity >= 4 is permanently U, no matter how well the executable classes perform.
statement: PB-4: under Kleene conjunction with 5 of 8 classes blocked, every composite requirement of arity 4 or higher is permanently U, making the satisfaction family effectively inert for realistic multi-class requirements.

anchor: Zero_reasoned <=> no bot AND no U that the AGENT could still act on ... Zero_strict => Zero_reasoned => Zero_weak ... Status upgraded 2026-09-02 ... Exhaustive check over 1,620,000 assignments ... found 0 counterexamples
statement: Introduces the Zero_reasoned closure reading (closes only on non-agent-actionable U) and its implication chain with strict and weak, later upgraded from observed to machine-checked derived across 1,620,000 assignments with zero counterexamples.
